tasks.short: Establish the fence line and check utility information

steps.what: Establish the proposed fence location on the actual site with the customer and existing boundary information
inputs: actual site and existing boundary information

steps.what: Gather and read the actual available cable and water-line information relevant to the proposed fence line
inputs: existing utility-owner information and site records
outputs: source-checked utility information and unresolved gaps

steps.what: Compare utility information with the actual site and resolve uncertainty before deciding whether the proposed fence location can be used
inputs: source-checked utility information and unresolved gaps
outputs: checked fence location or unresolved utility conflict requiring further verification

tasks.design: Use native project-document references in {DOCS} to find the actual available utility records for the proposed fence line. The erector establishes the line on site and checks uncertainty with the actual evidence; a map lookup never certifies that an area is free of services.
tasks.previous_blocker: Relevant utility records can be scattered among project documents.
tasks.enabler_now: Native site and version indexing can reduce document navigation.
tasks.still_hard: A missing line on a record is not evidence that no cable or pipe exists.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize conflicting site evidence and stop an unsupported location decision.

ambition.what: No automated utility clearance or excavation authorization.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: document indexing can assist utility-information retrieval but cannot establish the absence of buried services.

assumptions: Boundary includes fence-line establishment, actual information gathering and site comparison. No utility request send or construction release is performed by the proposed tool.

Customer and site owner supply existing boundary context; utility owners supply actual records with area, source and date. The erector checks applicability in s2 and gaps in s3. Missing records require manual further verification, not inferred clearance.
Native document indexing first. Shares are provisional scenarios; only retrieval navigation changes. Gross 4.5 minus 0.5 upkeep gives 4 net. Actual location and uncertainty decisions stay retained.
unknowns: Available utility information and actual retrieval burden
Local process for obtaining further utility verification
research_questions: Does indexing reduce retrieval without making incomplete records appear to be an all-clear?

already_counted.description: Verify retrieved utility records and their applicability

incremental.description: Maintain site document references and version checks

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Zero where records are already organized; up to 2.5% with smaller navigation gains than central 4% net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Discuss fencing needs and issue a checked quote

steps.what: Discuss fencing needs, preferred materials, gates and practical constraints with the customer
Measure the actual fence run and assess access, ground and installation requirements
outputs: measured dimensions and selected installation assumptions

steps.what: Estimate material quantities, labor and price from the measured run and selected construction assumptions
inputs: measured dimensions and selected installation assumptions
current material prices and approved labor rates
outputs: calculated fence estimate with explicit assumptions

steps.what: Prepare the customer quote with scope, itemized prices, assumptions and exclusions
inputs: calculated fence estimate with explicit assumptions

steps.what: Check the completed quote against measured scope and estimate and authorize the final price and recipient
inputs: measured dimensions and selected installation assumptions
calculated fence estimate with explicit assumptions
outputs: checked final quote and customer recipient

steps.what: Send the checked final fence quote to the customer
inputs: checked final quote and customer recipient

tasks.design: Configure native fence estimating rules in the estimating tool {OTHER}, then fill the quote in {DOCS} from those calculated lines. The erector discusses needs, measures the site and checks the complete price and scope before sending the exact quote through {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated quantity entry and quote layout take time after site assessment.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured quantity formulas and fixed quote templates can reuse measured inputs.
tasks.still_hard: Ground conditions or access may invalidate a standard installation allowance.
tasks.human_edge: Choose practical assumptions and explain the quote's scope to the customer.

ambition.what: Compare a second customer-requested fence material with the same measured site assumptions.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1-5; prices, quoting rights and staff consultation

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: estimating formulas and quote templates can reuse measured dimensions and price tables without replacing site assessment or commercial approval.

assumptions: OTHER is fence estimating software. Boundary covers customer discussion, site assessment, estimate, written quote, final check and send. Customer acceptance and materials purchasing are separate.

Erector supplies measured length, height, gate count, chosen construction and installation assumptions in s2. Purchasing supplies current material unit prices and the business supplies labor rates. Missing or unusual conditions require manual estimate adjustment in s3.

Native estimating configuration first. Shares are provisional; only repeated human estimate preparation and quote layout change, not existing calculator runtime. No model supplies quantities, rates or prices.

Final price checking is ordinary quoting authority, assumed already held by this role. Any edit or recipient change requires another check. The short send is 1% fully retained; gross 20 minus 1 upkeep yields 19 net.
unknowns: Current estimating automation and actual repeated-entry effort
research_questions: Can measured-input reuse reduce estimate and quote effort without missing site-specific installation work?

already_counted.description: Review estimate preparation, quote layout and final price

incremental.description: Maintain tested quantity rules, prices and quote template

approvals.approved_version: checked final quote and recipient from s5; any edit voids approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Zero where estimating and templates already reuse inputs; up to 13% where unusual ground and manual adjustments reduce central 19% net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The erector retains site and customer judgement while native reference and estimating tools reduce repeated navigation and entry.
role.ambitious_version: Compare a customer-requested material alternative using the same verified site measurements and explicit scope.
